claims.claim: The child usually lives in Scotland.
claims.quote: Any adult with parental responsibilities and rights or a guardian can apply for Child Disability Payment on behalf of the child if the child: is under 16 lives in Scotland
claims.note: The main applicant rule names a child living in Scotland.

claims.claim: A child living in the EEA, Switzerland or Gibraltar may still qualify with a genuine and sufficient link to Scotland.
claims.quote: You can still apply if the child both: lives in the EEA, Switzerland or Gibraltar has a genuine and sufficient link to Scotland
claims.note: The page explicitly names the places and the required link.

claims.claim: For a child abroad, the UK must be responsible for paying the benefit.
claims.quote: Social Security Scotland will also need to make sure that the UK is the competent state to pay the child’s benefits.
claims.note: The page requires a UK competent-state check.

claims.claim: A child outside Scotland who is not in the qualifying EEA, Swiss or Gibraltar route cannot qualify through that route.
claims.quote: You can still apply if the child both: lives in the EEA, Switzerland or Gibraltar has a genuine and sufficient link to Scotland
claims.note: The stated exception requires residence in one of the listed places and a genuine link.
